sources: Wed Aug 26 2026 run, capturing Tuesday Aug 25 closes. THEME: the war premium came out of crude in two brutal sessions while everything else barely moved - this is a commodity unwind, not a risk-off event. CRUDE COLLAPSED: Brent 87.12 Aug 25 (OilPrice.com board; TradingEconomics showed 86.33-86.94, treat as a close range not a settlement), DOWN 5.05 (-5.48%) from Monday's 92.17 and DOWN 7.7% from Friday - the entire move landed in the two sessions AFTER Treasury announced 'Operation Economic Outcast' on Iran. Two drivers, same direction: the sanctions set no deadline and designated no major Chinese bank (China takes 80%+ of Iran's seaborne crude), and Pakistan's Field Marshal Asim Munir spent Monday in Tehran carrying a sanctions-relief proposal. Neither removes a barrel; both remove fear. Murban's premium to Brent - the cleanest read on Hormuz risk, since those barrels bypass the strait - roughly HALVED from north of 11 dollars. Brent fell harder than WTI two sessions running: that is a risk premium unwinding, not oil repricing. NOTE: crude kept falling into Aug 26 on reports of an Iran-Oman 'temporary joint maritime corridor' (WTI 80.47 intraday, -2.3%), so this print is already stale to the downside. THE FLOOR IS STILL PHYSICAL: Hormuz flows 4.9mb/d in Q2 vs 21.6mb/d in Q4 2025, shut-in production 5.5mb/d in July, EIA projects a further 3.8mb/d Q3 inventory draw. And the pump has not moved: US diesel 5.620/gal, UP 15c in a week, diesel crack near a record 102/bbl, distillate stocks the thinnest for the time of year since 1996. The binding constraint has moved downstream from crude to refining. VOL TICKED UP BUT STAYS BENIGN: VIX 15.85 Aug 25 (+4.76% d/d, Investing/TradingEconomics), UP from 15.13 and from ~14.25 a week ago but still near 2026 lows. MOVE ~73 Aug 24 (Cboe Insights, 54th percentile) - it reversed a two-week decline but is unstressed; VXTLT jumped from the 13th to the 32nd percentile, so what anxiety exists sits in the long end, not equities. THE LONG END IS STILL THE STORY: 10Y-2Y +0.47 Aug 25 (FRED T10Y2Y), essentially unchanged w/w (0.46 Aug 24, 0.50 Aug 21). The 30Y touched 5.33% intraweek, highest since 2007, before Bessent doubled the Treasury buyback programme to 4bn; Aug 25 10Y 4.706%, 30Y 5.237%. That an intervention was needed at all remains the most notable fact on the board and is captured by none of the 19 gauges. CREDIT SHRUGGED: HY OAS 269bp Aug 24 (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2), DOWN 6bp from the 275 carried last run and flat vs 270 a week ago - last week's widening did not extend. Credit has now ignored the UMich collapse, a 30% oil round-trip and a 2007-high long bond. STILL THE PLACE THE FIRST CRACK WOULD SHOW. DOLLAR FLAT AT A THREE-MONTH LOW: DXY 98.89 Aug 25 (Investing.com; TradingEconomics 98.96, -0.04% d/d), DOWN from 99.80 a week ago, ahead of PCE. GROWTH MIX UNCHANGED: gold ~4,698/oz Aug 25 (Yahoo Finance; Dec futures opened 4,710, TradingEconomics 4,637 - a ~70 spread across venues, gold at a 3-month high), copper 6.62/lb (Investing.com). Copper/gold 1.41, FLAT vs Friday and DOWN from 1.50 a week ago. Gold is still doing all the work. BREAKEVENS: T5YIFR 2.33% Aug 25 (FRED), 2.32 Aug 24, 2.32 a week ago - flat, and notably NOT falling with the 8-dollar drop in crude, which supports reading both legs of the oil move as supply-side rather than demand. FREIGHT CAME OFF THE HIGHS: BDTI ~2961 Aug 24, DERIVED from StockQ (YTD +124.49% vs +127.75% at the Aug 21 print of 3004; MA5 2956, MA20 2711) - StockQ still exposes no dated numeric value, so this is an inference, not an assessment. Still the deepest red on the board and ~2.2x where it started the year. NFCI -0.559 for the week ending Aug 14 (FRED, updated Aug 19) - the Aug 26 print was NOT yet on FRED at run time, value carried. With HY at 269 and vol near lows, conditions have not tightened. CARRIED, NO NEW PRINT: EUR/USD 3M xccy -10bp (no free dated quote, no funding-stress event in the window). SOFR-OIS ~2bp. Initial claims 206k for the week ending Aug 15 (DOL); NEXT PRINT AUG 27. Building permits 1,443k July SAAR. LEI y/y ~-1.1% (Conference Board: +0.2% m/m July to 99.5, six-month growth rate positive for the first time in over four years, but y/y negative for four-plus years). ISM Manufacturing 55.6 July (four-year high, seventh straight month of expansion); August prints Sep 1. UMich 51.0 August PRELIMINARY (-8% m/m, current conditions 51.8, expectations 50.6, year-ahead inflation expectations 4.3%); FINAL LANDS AUG 28 and is the week's key release. Sahm Rule -0.03 July, no labour trigger; August prints Sep 4. Global liquidity 1=stable: Fed ended QT Dec 2025, ECB still shrinking through 2026 - divergent, net neutral. WATCH: NFCI and PCE, claims Aug 27, UMich final Aug 28, whether Brent breaks 85 on the Oman corridor talks, ISM Sep 1.
